title: Roald Amundsen's birth chart
metaDescription: Roald Amundsen's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 24.1° Cancer. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Tightest of all, the Sun holds a conjunction to Venus at 0.1° — close enough to weld identity to taste. A conjunction is the least negotiable aspect in the scheme — no distance to argue across, so the pair arrives as a single instinct.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At the noon reference the Sun sits 24.1° into Cancer — the third decan, which the old scheme hands to Jupiter. Same sign, different decan, different chart.

blocks.title: The personal registers
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 15.3° Leo; Venus stands at 24.2° Cancer; Mars stands at 8.1° Cancer. The tradition reads thought that arrives already in motion from Mercury, attraction that works by atmosphere from Venus, effort that surges when it matters from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Start where the chart is tightest — the Sun conjunction Venus, 0.1° of separation. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding. Behind it, Venus square Neptune at 2.1°, and the Sun square Neptune at 2.1° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. The unknown hour cannot unmake any of this: every aspect named survived all twenty-five samples of the day.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: The oldest layer of the scheme — seven planets, four conditions — flags two placements in this chart. Mars in Cancer at 8.1° is in fall — the tradition’s uphill placement, strength earned rather than given; Saturn in Capricorn at 17.5° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 9 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 4 fire, 3 water, 2 earth by element and 5 cardinal, 4 fixed by modality. Fire weights a chart toward initiative — starting, asserting, spending energy to find out what happens. No settled placement falls in air — an absence the tradition treats as information, not as a defect. Saturn was retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon is genuinely open
blocks.text: The Moon crossed from Scorpio into Sagittarius during that day at the birthplace, travelling 14.0° between one midnight and the next. Without a recorded hour there is no honest way to say which side it was on, so this reading does not say. The Moon sign is a real question here, not a rounding error, and it needs a birth time nobody has published.
